title: Experiment config caching + propagation controls (staleness bounds, fallback behavior)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
We need explicit caching + propagation semantics for route experiment configs so the data plane can apply experiments deterministically without introducing new failure modes. This ticket defines staleness limits, cache behavior, and fallback behavior when config is unavailable/unparseable/out-of-date.

Key requirements:
- Define cache layers + invalidation strategy for experiment configs consumed by the policy engine/router (incl. multi-process / multi-pod behavior).
- Define staleness bounds (max age / version skew) and what the router should do when config is stale.
- Define fallback behavior when config is unavailable (control plane outage, propagation lag, cache miss, etc.).
- Emit metrics for propagation lag + stale-config decisions; make them usable for SLOs/alerts + Console guardrail banners.

References:
- Confluence: experiment-service overview (APIs, storage model, caching strategy, failure modes)
- ADR-047 deterministic bucketing (needs stable inputs regardless of cache refresh)
- ADR-048 metrics attribution schema (must be present even when falling back)

Non-goals:
- Cross-region active rebalancing of allocations.
- Full stat-sig analysis engine.
comments: 2025-01-23 (Ethan Park): Creating as P0 for Phase 1. Router/policy engine needs a consistent story for what happens during control plane brownouts. We also need to avoid a silent fail-open that destroys attribution quality for Console.

2025-01-28 (Jordan Lee): +1. Deterministic bucketing depends on stable config inputs. If config refresh is inconsistent across pods, we’ll see "variant flapping" for the same stickiness key. Need a staleness/version strategy that avoids assigning different variants for the same user within a short window.

2025-02-02 (Michael Nguyen): Proposal:
- Control plane publishes experiment configs with monotonically increasing config_version.
- Data plane keeps:
  (a) local in-memory cache (per process) with TTL
  (b) shared cache (per node/pod) optional, but keep it simple for v1
- Refresh strategy: async background poll with jitter; no synchronous fetch on request path.
- Staleness bounds:
  - soft bound: warn + emit metric when cache_age > 60s
  - hard bound: stop applying experiments when cache_age > 10m OR config_version fetch fails for >10m (fail-safe)
- Fallback: if config unavailable/stale beyond hard bound -> do NOT run the experiment evaluator; proceed with normal routing/canary/fallback policies.
- Attribution: emit experiment_id/variant_id only when evaluator ran successfully. Also emit a separate "experiment_attribution_drop_reason" metric tag (bounded cardinality).

Open question: fail-open vs fail-closed. I’m leaning to fail-closed (no experiment) once hard stale, to avoid skew + confusing results.

Will sync with SRE on the 10m number (might be too high/low).

2025-02-04 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE: prefer explicit fail-closed after a bounded staleness threshold. During outages we want predictable behavior and the ability to alert on it.

Suggested thresholds:
- soft: cache_age > 90s (page only if sustained)
- hard: cache_age > 5m -> stop applying experiments

Also add metrics:
- experiment_config_cache_age_seconds (p50/p95 across pods)
- experiment_config_fetch_errors_total
- experiment_config_stale_decisions_total{reason}
- experiment_config_version (gauge) so we can compare across regions

Make sure we can correlate with propagation lag dashboards; don’t blow up cardinality.

2025-02-07 (Michael Nguyen): Update after implementation review w/ Vikram + Jordan:
- We’ll keep the request path purely read-only and lock-free: evaluator reads an immutable snapshot updated by background refresh.
- Refresh cadence: every 15s + jitter; on failure, exponential backoff capped at 60s.
- Staleness:
  - soft: > 90s emit warning metric
  - hard: > 5m -> evaluator disabled for that route’s experiments until config refresh succeeds
- Fallback semantics clarified:
  - If stale>hard or config parse/validation failure: skip experiment evaluation; proceed with existing routing policy engine (including canary + fallback policies).
  - If evaluator skipped, do not attach experiment_id/variant_id to request context.
  - Emit a single bounded drop-reason dimension (stale_hard | parse_error | fetch_error | disabled_flag).

NOTE: This does mean results have a visible attribution drop during outages, which is expected and will be shown in dashboards (better than silently mixing traffic).

Next: wire propagation lag metric + add runbook notes for debugging skew vs stale fallback.

2025-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure the hard-stale behavior is discoverable. We should surface a banner/indicator in Console results view for "Experiment paused due to stale config" (or at least make it obvious in the health dashboard). This will reduce support tickets about "results stopped updating".

2025-02-24 (Michael Nguyen): Landed metrics + alert hooks in follow-up PRs (see links in related work). Added a "config snapshot" debug dump to internal logs so oncall can verify which version a pod is serving.

One more tweak from SRE: treat "version skew" across pods > 2 versions as a warning (not a hard stop), because rollouts can produce temporary skew during deploys. We’ll alert if sustained > 10m.
2025-03-12 (Connor O'Brien): Marking done for Phase 1 readiness. Included in beta enablement checklist. Follow-up work (ENG-9033) will tune alert thresholds after first two beta customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Data plane reads experiment configs from an immutable snapshot updated asynchronously; no synchronous control-plane calls on request path.
2) Soft/hard staleness thresholds implemented and documented:
   - soft warning: cache_age > 90s (metrics only)
   - hard stop: cache_age > 5m OR repeated fetch/parse failure -> disable experiment evaluator until refresh succeeds.
3) Fallback behavior defined and implemented:
   - if evaluator disabled/unavailable -> skip experiments and proceed with normal routing/canary/fallback policies.
   - no experiment_id/variant_id added to request context when evaluator skipped.
4) Telemetry emitted:
   - propagation lag / cache age metric
   - stale decision counter with bounded reasons
   - fetch/parse error counters
5) Docs/notes added for oncall + debugging: how to confirm current config_version and differentiate stale fallback from true allocation skew.
6) Load/perf: refresh logic must not introduce tail latency regressions; evaluator read path must remain lock-free / constant-time.
notes:
Implementation details to keep in mind:
- Determinism: if config changes (allocations/variants), determinism is only guaranteed within a given config_version. During a rollout, a given stickiness key may map to a different variant after config_version increments; that’s acceptable and should be reflected as an audit event + visible change history.
- Avoid cache stampede: refresh uses jitter and backoff; no request-triggered fetch.
- Cardinality: drop-reason must be bounded and must NOT include experiment_id by default in high-volume metrics. Detailed breakdown should live in logs/traces sampled appropriately.
- Console expectations: during hard-stale, results may appear flat/paused; rely on health dashboard + attribution drop metrics to explain.
